item.title: Identifying an Element from a Two-Isotope Mass Spectrum
item.stimulus:
A pure sample of an unknown element X is analyzed in a mass spectrometer. Every peak in the spectrum comes from singly charged ions of single atoms of X. The mass of each isotope and the relative intensity of its peak are listed below.

Isotope mass (amu) | Relative intensity
62.93 | 100.0
64.93 | 44.61

Answer the following.

parts.prompt: Calculate the percent abundance of the isotope with mass 62.93 amu.

criteria.text: Calculates a percent abundance of 69.15% for the isotope with mass 62.93 amu.
criteria.evidence: Response divides the intensity of the 62.93 amu peak by the total intensity of both peaks (100.0 ÷ 144.61) and reports 69.15%.
criteria.fix: Add all the peak intensities, then divide the chosen peak's intensity by that total and multiply by 100.

parts.prompt: Calculate the average atomic mass of element X.

criteria.text: Calculates an average atomic mass of 63.55 amu.
criteria.evidence: Response computes a weighted average of the two isotope masses using their relative abundances or intensities, for example 0.6915 × 62.93 amu + 0.3085 × 64.93 amu, and reports 63.55 amu.
criteria.fix: Weight each isotope mass by its fractional abundance, add the products, and report the result in amu.

parts.prompt: Identify element X. Justify your answer.

criteria.text: Identifies X as copper (Cu) because the calculated average atomic mass, 63.55 amu, matches the atomic mass of copper on the periodic table.
criteria.evidence: Response names copper and links the average atomic mass from the previous part to the atomic mass listed for Cu.
criteria.fix: Compare your calculated average atomic mass with the periodic table and name the element whose atomic mass matches it.

parts.prompt: Atoms of the two isotopes of X have different masses. Explain this difference in terms of the numbers of protons and neutrons in the atoms.

criteria.text: Explains that atoms of both isotopes have the same number of protons (29) but atoms of the heavier isotope have 2 more neutrons.
criteria.evidence: Response states that the number of protons is the same in both isotopes (they are the same element) and that the 64.93 amu isotope has more neutrons (two more); it does not attribute the mass difference to protons or electrons.
criteria.fix: Isotopes of one element always share the same number of protons; explain any mass difference by a different number of neutrons.

item.model_answer:
(a) Total intensity = 100.0 + 44.61 = 144.61. Percent abundance of the 62.93 amu isotope = (100.0 ÷ 144.61) × 100% = 69.15%.

(b) The 64.93 amu isotope has an abundance of 100% − 69.15% = 30.85%. Average atomic mass = 0.6915 × 62.93 amu + 0.3085 × 64.93 amu = 43.52 amu + 20.03 amu = 63.55 amu.

(c) X is copper (Cu). The average atomic mass of 63.55 amu matches the atomic mass of copper on the periodic table.

(d) Both isotopes are copper, so every atom of each isotope has 29 protons. The isotope with mass 64.93 amu has two more neutrons (36) than the isotope with mass 62.93 amu (34), and the extra neutrons account for its greater mass.

item.title: Gallium Mass Spectrum: Abundances and Average Atomic Mass
item.stimulus:
A pure sample of gallium metal is vaporized and analyzed in a mass spectrometer. Only singly charged Ga+ ions reach the detector, and exactly two peaks are observed. The peak heights are reported relative to the tallest peak, which is set to 100.0. The isotopic masses are listed as the mass-to-charge ratio of each peak.

Peak | Mass of isotope (amu) | Relative intensity
1 | 68.926 | 100.0
2 | 70.925 | 66.4

Gallium has atomic number 31.
item.model_answer:
(a) Total relative intensity = 100.0 + 66.4 = 166.4. Fraction of peak 2 isotope = 66.4/166.4 = 0.399, so the percent abundance of gallium-71 is 39.9%. (Gallium-69 is then 60.1%.)

(b) Average atomic mass = (0.601)(68.926 amu) + (0.399)(70.925 amu) = 41.42 amu + 28.30 amu = 69.72 amu.

(c) The mass difference is caused by neutrons. Both isotopes have 31 protons, which is what makes them gallium. Gallium-69 has 69 − 31 = 38 neutrons and gallium-71 has 71 − 31 = 40 neutrons, so gallium-71 has two more neutrons, accounting for the extra 2 amu.

(d) The average atomic mass of the second sample is greater than 69.72 amu. Peak 2 is now a larger share of the total intensity, so the heavier isotope gallium-71 makes up a larger fraction of the atoms. Because average atomic mass is a weighted average of isotopic masses, increasing the abundance of the heavier isotope shifts the average toward 70.925 amu.
item.verification_python:
m1 = 68.926
m2 = 70.925
i1 = 100.0
i2 = 66.4
tot = i1 + i2
assert abs(tot - 166.4) < 1e-9
f2 = i2 / tot
f1 = i1 / tot
assert abs(round(f2 * 100, 1) - 39.9) < 1e-9
assert abs(round(f1 * 100, 1) - 60.1) < 1e-9
avg = f1 * m1 + f2 * m2
assert abs(round(avg, 2) - 69.72) < 1e-9
assert abs(round(avg, 1) - 69.7) < 1e-9
avg_rounded = 0.601 * m1 + 0.399 * m2
assert abs(round(0.601 * m1, 2) - 41.42) < 1e-9
assert abs(round(0.399 * m2, 2) - 28.30) < 1e-9
assert abs(round(avg_rounded, 2) - 69.72) < 1e-9
assert 69 - 31 == 38 and 71 - 31 == 40
f2b = 80.0 / 180.0
avg2 = (1 - f2b) * m1 + f2b * m2
assert avg2 > avg
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

criteria.fix: Convert relative peak heights to abundances by dividing each height by the sum of all peak heights, not by the tallest peak.

item.title: Average Atomic Mass from a Three-Peak Mass Spectrum
item.stimulus:
A pure sample of an unknown element X was vaporized and analyzed in a mass spectrometer. Every peak arises from a singly charged monatomic ion, X⁺. The spectrometer reports peak heights relative to the tallest peak, which is set to 100.0. The data are summarized below.

Peak | Isotopic mass (amu) | Relative peak height
1 | 27.977 | 100.0
2 | 28.976 | 5.06
3 | 29.974 | 3.36

Assume each peak height is proportional to the relative abundance of that isotope in the sample.
item.model_answer:
(a) Total peak height = 100.0 + 5.06 + 3.36 = 108.42. Fraction for peak 1 = 100.0 / 108.42 = 0.922, so the percent abundance is 92.2%.

(b) Fractions: peak 1 = 0.9223, peak 2 = 5.06/108.42 = 0.0467, peak 3 = 3.36/108.42 = 0.0310.
Average atomic mass = (27.977)(0.9223) + (28.976)(0.0467) + (29.974)(0.0310) = 25.803 + 1.352 + 0.929 = 28.09 amu.

(c) An average atomic mass of 28.09 amu matches silicon, Si, on the periodic table. Silicon has 14 protons. The peak 2 isotope has mass number 29, so it has 29 − 14 = 15 neutrons.

(d) The claim is incorrect. All three peaks come from the same element, silicon, so every atom has 14 protons; a different proton number would mean a different element. The masses differ because the isotopes contain different numbers of neutrons (14, 15 and 16). The average atomic mass is a weighted average, and the 27.977 amu isotope makes up about 92% of the atoms, so the average lies close to 28 amu rather than 29 amu.
item.verification_python:
import math
m=[27.977,28.976,29.974]
h=[100.0,5.06,3.36]
tot=sum(h)
assert abs(tot-108.42)<1e-9
f=[x/tot for x in h]
assert abs(f[0]*100-92.2)<0.05
assert abs(f[1]-0.0467)<0.0001
assert abs(f[2]-0.0310)<0.0001
avg=sum(a*b for a,b in zip(m,f))
assert abs(avg-28.09)<0.005
assert abs(27.977*0.9223-25.803)<0.001
assert abs(28.976*0.0467-1.352)<0.001
assert abs(29.974*0.0310-0.929)<0.001
assert abs(28.0855-28.0855)<1e-9
Z=14
assert round(m[1])-Z==15
assert [round(x)-Z for x in m]==[14,15,16]
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')

criteria.text: Percent abundance of the 27.977 amu isotope is 92.2%
criteria.evidence: Divides 100.0 by the sum of all peak heights (108.42) and reports about 92.2%, or the fraction 0.922.
criteria.fix: Add all peak heights first, then divide the peak of interest by that total; relative heights are not percentages.

parts.prompt: Calculate the average atomic mass of element X, in amu, reported to the correct number of significant figures. Show your work.

criteria.text: Sets up a weighted average of isotopic masses using each isotope's fractional abundance
criteria.evidence: Shows each isotopic mass multiplied by its fractional abundance (or by its peak height, then divided by 108.42) and summed.
criteria.fix: Multiply each isotopic mass by its fraction of the total peak height, then add the products.

criteria.text: Average atomic mass is 28.09 amu
criteria.evidence: Reports 28.09 amu (or 28.1 amu) consistent with a correct weighted-average setup.
criteria.fix: Carry unrounded fractions through the weighted sum and round only the final answer, keeping the precision of the peak heights.

parts.prompt: Identify element X and state the number of neutrons in the atoms responsible for peak 2.

criteria.text: Identifies X as silicon and states that peak 2 atoms have 15 neutrons
criteria.evidence: Names silicon (Si), linked to the calculated average atomic mass of about 28.09 amu matching the periodic table, and gives 15 neutrons from mass number 29 minus 14 protons.
criteria.fix: Match your calculated average mass to the periodic table, then subtract the atomic number from the rounded isotopic mass to get neutrons.

parts.prompt: A student claims that the three peaks have different masses because the atoms contain different numbers of protons. Evaluate this claim, and explain why the average atomic mass of X is much closer to 28 amu than to 29 amu.

criteria.text: Rejects the claim: isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons; average is near 28 because the 27.977 amu isotope is by far most abundant
criteria.evidence: States all peaks are the same element so have 14 protons, mass differences come from differing neutron counts, and the weighted average is dominated by the roughly 92% abundant lightest isotope.
criteria.fix: Remember proton number fixes element identity; isotopes differ only in neutrons, and the weighted average lies nearest the most abundant isotope.

item.title: Silicon Isotopes from a Single-Element Mass Spectrum
item.stimulus:
A pure sample of an unknown element X was analyzed in a mass spectrometer. Only singly charged monatomic ions of X were detected. The spectrum shows three peaks. The mass of the isotope for each peak and the relative peak height are listed below. Relative heights are scaled so that the tallest peak equals 100.0.

Isotope | Isotopic mass (amu) | Relative peak height
X-28 | 27.977 | 100.0
X-29 | 28.976 | 5.06
X-30 | 29.974 | 3.36

Assume that peak height is proportional to the relative abundance of each isotope in the sample.
item.model_answer:
(a) Total peak height = 100.0 + 5.06 + 3.36 = 108.42. Percent abundance of X-28 = (100.0 / 108.42) × 100 = 92.23%.

(b) The fractional abundances are 100.0/108.42 = 0.9223, 5.06/108.42 = 0.04667, and 3.36/108.42 = 0.03099.
Average atomic mass = (27.977)(0.9223) + (28.976)(0.04667) + (29.974)(0.03099) = 28.09 amu.

(c) Element X is silicon (Si). The average atomic mass calculated in part (b), 28.09 amu, matches the atomic mass of Si on the periodic table. It does not match Al (26.98) or P (30.97).

(d) Every atom of silicon has 14 protons, and the number of protons is what identifies the element. The isotopes differ only in their number of neutrons. X-28 has 28 − 14 = 14 neutrons, X-29 has 29 − 14 = 15 neutrons, and X-30 has 30 − 14 = 16 neutrons. Each extra neutron adds about 1 amu, so the ions reach the detector at three different masses.

(e) The average atomic mass is a weighted average, not a simple average of the three isotopic masses. The X-28 peak is much taller than the other two, so X-28 makes up about 92% of the atoms. X-29 and X-30 together make up only about 8%. Because most atoms have a mass near 28 amu, the average, 28.09 amu, lies very close to 28 and not near 29.
item.verification_python:
masses=[27.977,28.976,29.974]
h=[100.0,5.06,3.36]
T=sum(h)
assert abs(T-108.42)<1e-9
pct=h[0]/T*100
assert abs(pct-92.23)<0.01
fr=[x/T for x in h]
assert abs(fr[0]-0.9223)<5e-5 and abs(fr[1]-0.04667)<5e-6 and abs(fr[2]-0.03099)<5e-6
avg=sum(m*f for m,f in zip(masses,fr))
assert abs(avg-28.0855)<0.001
assert round(avg,2)==28.09
assert abs(sum(fr[1:])*100-7.77)<0.05
Z=14
assert [28-Z,29-Z,30-Z]==[14,15,16]
assert abs(avg-28.09)<abs(avg-26.98) and abs(avg-28.09)<abs(avg-30.97)
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')
